title: Portaki module public listing (listing.json)
description: What a host reads in the catalogue before installing the module. Optional: without listing.json the listing is written in the developer dashboard. With it, portaki publish sends it on every run and it overwrites the dashboard version. Every text is a dictionary keyed by language; fr is the fallback language and must always be written — the catalogue serves a listing only once its French tagline and description are filled.

$schema.description: The schema this file follows — lets an editor offer completion and checks.

category.description: The moment of the stay the module belongs to: arrival (getting in, check-in), stay (life in the rental), around (the neighbourhood, outings), formalities (forms, rules, paperwork).

tagline.description: One sentence, shown on the catalogue card and the landing: what the module brings to a host. 90 characters at most — past that the card truncates.

description.description: The body of the listing: what the module does for the host and the guest, in a few sentences. Say what they see and do, not how it is built.

guestSurface.description: Only when the module shows something in the guest booklet: what the guest sees there. Omit it for a host-only module.

hostSurface.description: What the host sees and sets in the dashboard — the sheet, the tab, the card. Required: the landing page shows it.

configItems.description: What the host fills in, one entry per setting (e.g. "Temperature units"). Short labels, not sentences. Empty when there is nothing to configure.

capabilities.description: The data and connections the module consumes, and where each comes from.

label.description: What is consumed, as a host reads it (e.g. "Weather data", "Your Nuki account").

kind.description: pool: provided by Portaki, nothing to set up. byok: the host connects their own account or key. plan: included in a Portaki plan. module_contract: supplied by another module.

publishedLangs.description: The languages the listing appears in. fr is always added by the registry. A published language missing a tagline or description falls back to French.

i18nText.description: A text per language — keys among fr, en, es, de, it, nl.
